name: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank Ltd
title: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank Ltd - 543942 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Utkarsh SFB narrowed Q1 FY27 net loss to INR34 crore (down over 80% YoY and QoQ), with GNPA at 5.9% and credit cost at 2.3%.
summary.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 showed a clear turn: total disbursements rose 49% YoY, fresh slippages fell to about INR125 crore from INR170 crore in Q4 FY26, and GNPA improved to 5.9% (about 550 bps YoY, 160 bps QoQ). Cost of funds fell to 7.7%, and PPOP rose to INR64 crore from INR12 crore in Q4. Profitability is not yet normal; the bank is still loss-making, and CGFMU guarantee benefit of about INR75 crore supported the P&L. Management guided to 25-30% loan growth, NIM around 8% and ROE around 15% by FY28, while analysts pressed on the quality of the legacy book and the growth push.

financial_highlights.metric: Fresh slippages (net of recoveries and upgradations)
financial_highlights.change: vs ~INR170 crore QoQ and ~INR400 crore YoY
vs 5.3% in Q4 FY26 and 8.5% in Q1 FY26
about fivefold vs INR12 crore in Q4 FY26

segments.name: Micro Banking (JLG + MBBL)
segments.commentary: JLG is 26% of gross loans (28% incl. BC JLG), down from 88% in March 2020. MBBL grew 147% YoY and 11% QoQ and is now above 30% of Micro Banking; Micro Banking slippages were INR68 crore vs INR153 crore in Q4, and Micro Banking SMA pools were 1.2%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Portfolio INR4,482 crore, up 12% YoY, with Micro LAP disbursement yield around 18%. GNPA about INR169 crore, or 3.8%.

segments.name: Housing / BBG / Gold / CV-CE
segments.commentary: Housing INR1,005 crore (up 8% YoY); BBG business banking up 40% YoY; gold loans about INR300 crore; used vehicles about 30% of CV/CE disbursements. Non-MFI GNPA about INR425 crore: MSME INR169 crore, CV&CE INR62 crore, WSL about INR30 crore, housing about INR49-50 crore.

segments.name: Liabilities
segments.commentary: Total deposits up 3% YoY; CASA up 15% and retail term deposits up 15% YoY. CASA ratio 22%, CASA plus retail TD 83% (vs 74% a year ago).

guidance_outlook: Loan book growth of 25-30% YoY (JLG and Micro Banking together 15-20%, JLG below 20%), with secured lending around 55% of portfolio.
NIM around 8%; ROE around 15% by FY28; management guided to a 2-digit ROE exiting FY27.
Credit cost guided at upper-end 3-3.5% going forward, described as conservative.
Tier 2 NCD raise of INR500 crore planned this year, expected to add about 250 bps to CRAR; no equity raise anticipated until at least end-FY27.
Early redemption of INR195 crore tranche at 12.5% coupon in mid-August, expected to save about INR20 crore.
Cost of funds to benefit further from progressive repricing over coming quarters.
NCLT hearing on the reverse merger of holding company UCL into the bank fixed for August 6, 2026; completion expected in the next few months, subject to NCLT.
Recoveries expected to pick up in Q2 and Q3 FY27, with about 1,100 JLG collection staff to be redeployed toward NPA recovery and write-offs.
capex_capacity: Around 1,100 branches; strategy is productivity over branch expansion. Headcount rationalised by about 1,700.
New LMS switchover completed; a new core banking system is about to launch; Utkarsh 2.0 technology transformation under way.
Collections workforce for JLG and MBBL exceeds 1,200; JLG collection headcount about 1,100, with a specialised call centre for overdue accounts.
demand_pricing: Industry JLG portfolio reportedly down about 30%; management says it will grow JLG only in its core geography, using partners outside it.
MBBL disbursements are about 99.9% existing customers with 2-3 prior cycles; a small pilot is open to new-to-bank customers.
Retail term deposit card rates cut: senior citizen peak 9.1% now 8.25%; general citizen 8.5% now 8.1%.
Q4 FY26 disbursements grew 30% YoY; Q1 FY27 disbursements grew 49% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned JLG portfolio run-down and the overall growth outlook for this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects JLG to hold around 25% of the book over the next 2-3 years, with Micro Banking plus business loans growing 15-20%, overall loan growth 25-30%, and JLG growth below 20%. Sarjukumar said the book will keep growing rather than run down, with the JLG/Micro Banking cap around 25%.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost and NPA guidance applies for the rest of FY27, and are further fundraises planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit cost guided at the upper end of 3-3.5%, described as conservative. The INR500 crore Tier 2 NCD adds about 250 bps to CRAR, while the INR195 crore 12.5% tranche is being redeemed early in mid-August, saving about INR20 crore. No equity raise is expected until at least end-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the asset quality of the post-guardrail book and how is CGFMU coverage positioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Post-April 2025 book is the majority of outstanding JLG book with GNPA of about 1.85-1.9%. CGFMU coverage is 60% for disbursements up to Q4 FY26 and about 80% including Q1 FY27 disbursements.

qa_highlights.question: How is MBBL sourced and underwritten, and is it going to new-to-bank customers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 99.9% of MBBL is existing customers with 2-3 prior cycles; new-to-bank is a small pilot of no more than about 100-200 accounts. MBBL outstanding is about INR2,246 crore, of which INR2,036 crore is post April 2025, with only 0.3% NPA in that pool. A separate underwriting team and a dedicated MBBL collection team are used.

qa_highlights.question: Why are recoveries slow, and how much of the slippage/NPA pool is in Micro Banking?
qa_highlights.answer: Slow retail recoveries are due to SARFAESI-linked legacy cases, with processes taking 6-7 months to auction. About INR28 crore of the recoveries pool was from Micro Banking. Recoveries are expected to pick up in Q2 and Q3, with about 1,100 JLG collection staff being redeployed to recoveries and write-offs.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the growth guidance given weak Q1 growth and how credible is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to Q4 FY26 disbursements up 30% YoY and Q1 FY27 up 49%, with H2 expected to carry the 25% growth target. Govind Singh said the 25-30% range is partly because write-offs shrink the reported book and the base is small after two years of no growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why is PPOP growing slowly and what is the path to profitability and cost-to-income?
qa_highlights.answer: PPOP moved from negative about INR44 crore in December to INR12 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR64 crore in Q1 FY27. Management expects cost-to-income to improve as income recovers with flat costs, with 2-digit ROE exiting FY27 and about 15% ROE in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the bank keep growing microfinance, and what is the risk weight on incremental MFI loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will keep MFI at about 25% of the book. Under CGFMU, only about INR15 of every INR100 of incremental MFI book gets zero risk weight, because the benefit is capped at 15% of crystallised disbursements; the remaining INR85 carries risk weight.

risks_watch: Asset quality of the legacy book: GNPA 5.9% and Micro Banking SMA pools at 1.2%; recoveries have been slow and management expects them to pick up only in Q2 and Q3 FY27.
Growth push versus the book: 25-30% loan growth guidance against JLG growth below 20% and an industry JLG portfolio reported down about 30%. An analyst challenged whether growth is the right focus.
Credit cost guided at 3-3.5% for the rest of the year, against 2.3% in Q1 that was helped by about INR75 crore of CGFMU mitigation; watch for the CGFMU benefit fading.
Profitability: still a net loss of INR34 crore; PPOP of INR64 crore needs to rise further to reach 2-digit ROE by Q4 FY27; cost-to-income remains elevated.

Funding and capital: INR500 crore Tier 2 NCD to add about 250 bps CRAR; early redemption of the INR195 crore 12.5% tranche in mid-August; the UCL reverse merger is pending NCLT, with the hearing set for August 6, 2026.
Non-MFI GNPA of about INR425 crore (MSME INR169 crore at 3.8%); management agreed to disclose segment-wise GNPA from next quarter.
key_quotes: While profitability has not yet fully normalized, the significant reduction in losses and the strengthening of underlying business drivers reinforce our confidence that the bank is moving in the right direction.
We are aiming for a loan book growth of 25% to 30% , with the secured lending comprising ~55% of the portfolio, maintaining NIM of around 8% and delivering a ROE of ~15% by FY28.
So, if we are able to do even 70% to 80% of the capability of our branches, I think we can do much, much more than this.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on momentum (disbursements, collections, cost of funds, PPOP), but cautious on profitability, which management says is not yet normal. Under pressure on the MFI legacy book and growth, management was defensive and gave long answers, and it left the NPA provision question open during the call.

adds.what: New core banking system about to launch (technology, not physical capacity)
Utkarsh 2.0 technology transformation under way (no capacity figure given)

growth.why: Loan book growth guided at 25-30% YoY for FY27 (midpoint 27.5%), but the bank is shifting to productivity over branch expansion (about 1,100 branches, headcount cut by about 1,700), no physical capacity additions are announced, and JLG disbursements grew only 5% YoY amid an industry JLG decline.
